key_insight: Conditioning 3D generation on an existing 3D shape (via a new VecSet-based mechanism) enables controlled regeneration — allowing enhancement, reconstruction, and editing rather than one-shot, uncontrollable generation.
problem_solved: Many 3D generators convert text or images to a single output with limited controllability; this paper addresses the need to refine or regenerate 3D geometry given an initial shape and additional 2D evidence.
method: Formulate 3D regeneration as a conditional generation problem: the model is conditioned on an initial 3D shape plus optional 2D images.
Introduce VecSet-based conditioning to fuse geometric priors from the input shape with image cues, allowing coherent updates to geometry.
Provide a unified framework that supports multiple tasks (enhancement, reconstruction, editing) by regenerating geometry rather than generating from scratch.
impact: Enables practical, controllable workflows for 3D asset improvement and editing — useful for reconstruction pipelines, content creation, and any system that needs iterative shape refinement from images and partial meshes.
visual_elements: Before/after gallery: initial 3D shape vs. regenerated output (several examples showing enhancement and edits).
Pipeline diagram: inputs (initial 3D + 2D images) → VecSet conditioning block → regenerator → output 3D geometry.
VecSet illustration: how vector-set conditioning merges spatial features from the shape and image cues (iconic vectors and attention arrows).
Use-case grid: small panels for enhancement, reconstruction, and editing showing typical inputs and outputs.
paper_authors: Geon Yeong Park, Roman Shapovalov, Rakesh Ranjan, Jong Chul Ye, Andrea Vedaldi
